Tosafot on Bava Batra 111a:11:1.english: This—its measure is like [that of] a sack - And if you ask: Is it worse than the rags (matlaniyot) in the chapter "Lo Yachpor" (above, Bava Batra 20a, and there), where we established [the case] as being like [a piece of] sackcloth, and even so their measure is three [handbreadths] by three? And one can answer that there we establish it as being like a sack only in the sense that they are not fit for a craftsman to wipe off the blood; but this [material] is far too coarse.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 111a:5:1.hebrew: קל וחומר לשכינה י"ד - אור"ת דלכך נקט י"ד, משום דאמר בהמפלת (נדה דף לא.): שלשה שותפין יש באדם: הקדוש ברוך הוא, אביו ואמו, ונותן בו הקב"ה כנגד שניהן. אבל קשה קצת, דאם כן אין זה קל וחומר, דמן הדין יש להיות כנגד שניהן. ועוד אמר בספרי בתוספתא: קל וחומר למלך וכהן י"ד. פירוש: משה רבינו שהיה מלך וכהן גדול, ששימש שבעת ימי המילואים. ואמשה רבינו אמאי נקט י"ד? ודוחק לומר דמלך היינו הקדוש ברוך הוא וכהן משה. ורבינו חיים כהן מפרש: קל וחומר לשכינה יותר מעט מז', וכיון דאפיקתיה מז' דהיינו הסגר, אוקמה אשני הסגרות. וכן משמע באבות:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 111a:5:1.english: A kal vachomer for the Divine Presence: fourteen - Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Gemara] specified fourteen because it says in [the chapter] Hamafelet (Niddah 31a): There are three partners in a person: the Holy One, blessed be He, his father, and his mother; and the Holy One, blessed be He, gives in him a share corresponding to both of them. But this is somewhat difficult, for if so, this is not a kal vachomer, since by right it should be [fourteen], corresponding to both of them. Furthermore, it says in the Sifrei, in the Tosefta: A kal vachomer for a king and a priest: fourteen. Explanation: [this refers to] Moses our teacher, who was a king and a high priest, for he served during the seven days of the inauguration. But regarding Moses our teacher, why did it specify fourteen? And it is forced to say that "king" means the Holy One, blessed be He, and "priest" means Moses. And Rabbeinu Chaim Kohen explains: the kal vachomer for the Divine Presence is slightly more than seven, and since you have removed it from seven — that is, [one period of] quarantine — you establish it at two quarantines. And so it is implied in Avot.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 111a:7:1.hebrew: מקיש מטה האם למטה האב וכו' - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי איצטריך לאשמועינן דבן קודם לבת בנכסי האם מהיקשא דמטות? תיפוק ליה מ"וירש אותה", דאמר לקמן (בבא בתרא דף קיג:): מקיש ירושה שניה לירושה ראשונה; מה ירושה ראשונה בן קודם לבת, אף ירושה שניה בן קודם לבת. דמיניה ילפינן לקמן דבני אחות קודמין לבנות אחות לירש בנכסי אחי האם ובנכסי אבי האם; דמה ירושה ראשונה, דהיינו בנכסי האב, בן קודם לבת — אף ירושה שניה, כגון בן הבת קודם לבת הבת בנכסי אבי האם. ואומר רשב"א דבן בנכסי האם היינו נמי ירושה ראשונה, הבאה מכח האם. ואי לאו דנפקא לן מהיקשא דמטות דבן קודם לבת בנכסי האם, היכי הוה שמעינן דקודם בנכסי אבי האם, דלא אתי אלא מכח היקשא דירושה ראשונה? הלכך איצטריך הכא למילף מעיקרא דבן קודם לבת בנכסי האם, שהיא ירושה ראשונה הבאה מכח האם, ושוב נפקא לן מהיקשא דלקמן דמקיש ירושה שניה לירושה ראשונה, בין ירושה שניה דאב בין ירושה שניה דאם. ור"י אומר דאע"ג דנפקא לן לקמן דבן קודם לבת בנכסי אבי האם, היינו משום דמכח אבוה דאימיה קאתי, ולא שמעינן מינה דקודם בנכסי האם עצמן. ואין נראה לרשב"א, דהא מכח דאבוה דאם לא ירית אלא ע"י משמוש, דנפלו לפני האם, והוא יורש את אמו. וא"ת: כיון דמהכא שמעינן דמהיקש דמטות דבן קודם לבת בנכסי האם, אמאי איצטריך כל הנך קראי — דלא תסוב נחלה, דאיירי בסיבת הבן, וקרא דאם אין לו בת, דאמר לקמן: בן הבת ובת הבת מנין? ת"ל "אם אין לו", עיין עליו — דמשמע דאתא לאשמועינן דבן יורש את אמו? ומיהו ההוא דואם אין לו בת איצטריך טובא, דלא הוה ידעינן שהיה בן הבת יורש כלל ע"י משמוש; והא דדרשינן נמי מוירש אותה להקיש ירושה שניה לראשונה, הוה מוקמינן בבת הבן דוקא. ולא תסוב נמי איצטריך: ללאו בסיבת הבן, ולא תסוב שני בסיבת הבעל; ולמאן דדריש בעל משארו, איצטריך לעבור עליו בשני לאוין. ומיהו קשה לרשב"א: דאמאי איצטריך הכא היקשא דמטות? כיון דשמעינן מ"ואם אין לו בת" ומ"לא תסוב" דבן יורש את אמו, תיפוק ליה מקל וחומר דבן קודם לבת! והשתא לא אמר "דיו", כיון דמפריך ק"ו. ומיהו פלוגתא היא בכיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כה.), דאיכא מ"ד אפילו היכא דמיפרך ק"ו אמר "דיו". ומיהו אפילו למ"ד לא אמר "דיו", איכא למימר דמילתא דאתיא בק"ו טרח וכתב לה קרא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 111a:7:1.english: "He equates the tribe of the mother with the tribe of the father," etc. - Rashba found this puzzling: Why was it necessary to teach us, from the analogy of the tribes, that a son takes precedence over a daughter in the mother's estate? Let us derive it from "and he shall inherit her," about which [the Gemara] says later (Bava Batra 113b): [Scripture] equates the second inheritance with the first inheritance; just as in the first inheritance a son takes precedence over a daughter, so too in the second inheritance a son takes precedence over a daughter. From this we derive later that the sons of a sister take precedence over the daughters of a sister in inheriting the estate of the mother's brothers and of the mother's father; for just as in the first inheritance, namely in the father's estate, a son takes precedence over a daughter, so too in the second inheritance, for example, a daughter's son takes precedence over a daughter's daughter in the estate of the mother's father. And Rashba says that a son inheriting his mother's estate is also a "first inheritance," which comes by way of the mother. And were it not that we derive from the analogy of the tribes that a son takes precedence over a daughter in the mother's estate, how would we have learned that he takes precedence in the estate of the mother's father, which comes only by virtue of the analogy to the first inheritance? Therefore, it was necessary here to learn first of all that a son takes precedence over a daughter in the mother's estate, which is a first inheritance that comes by way of the mother; and then we derive from the analogy later, which equates the second inheritance with the first inheritance, [that this applies to] both the second inheritance of a father and the second inheritance of a mother. But R. Yitzchak says that even though we derive later that a son takes precedence over a daughter in the estate of the mother's father, that is because he comes by virtue of his mother's father, and we do not learn from it that he takes precedence in the mother's own estate. This does not seem right to Rashba, for by virtue of the mother's father he inherits only by way of a "mishmush" [an indirect passing], since the estate fell first to the mother, and he inherits his mother. And if you ask: Since from here we learn, from the analogy of the tribes, that a son takes precedence over a daughter in the mother's estate, why were all those other verses necessary — "no inheritance shall move around [lo tisov]," which speaks of the movement [of the inheritance] through the son, and the verse "if he has no daughter," about which [the Gemara] says later: "From where do we know [the law of] a daughter's son and a daughter's daughter? Scripture teaches: 'if he has none'" — examine it — which implies that it comes to teach us that a son inherits his mother? However, the verse "if he has no daughter" was very much needed, for we would not have known at all that a daughter's son inherits by way of a "mishmush"; and as for the fact that we also expound from "and he shall inherit her" to equate the second inheritance with the first, we would have established that [as referring] only to a son's daughter. And "lo tisov" was also needed: [one] prohibition for the movement through the son, and a second "lo tisov" for the movement through the husband; and according to the one who expounds [that a] husband [inherits his wife] from "his kin [she'ero]," it was needed so that he would transgress two prohibitions. Nevertheless, there is a difficulty according to Rashba: Why was the analogy of the tribes needed here? Since we learn from "and if he has no daughter" and from "lo tisov" that a son inherits his mother, let us derive from a kal vachomer that a son takes precedence over a daughter! And now, [one] does not say "dayo" [it is enough to apply the law of the source], since the kal vachomer can be refuted. However, there is a dispute about this in [the chapter] "Keitzad HaRegel" (Bava Kamma 25a), for there is one who holds that even where the kal vachomer can be refuted, [one] says "dayo." But even according to the one who holds that [one] does not say "dayo," one can say that when a matter could be derived by a kal vachomer, Scripture nonetheless took the trouble to write it explicitly:
